get.description: Returns a list of xrefs and associated attributes that contain the query string for a given organism. Results are not restricted to exact matches. Optionally limit results to a specified number per data source, or by the type of attribute. See possible attribute types via /{organism}/attributeSet.

parameters.description: Restrict search by attribute name (case sensitive). Use GET /{organism}/attributeSet to find out which attributes are supported.
parameters.name: attrName

200.description: returns a tab-delimited list with the identifier, data source and descriptions found.

get.description: Returns the supported attributes to the given Organism.
Returns the attributes for a given identifier, data source, organism. Optionally display only a specified attribute

200.description: Returns a tab-delimited list with the attributes and their content

get.description: Returns `true` or `false` based on whether or not /{organism}/search/{query} is supported for a given organism.

Returns `true` or `false` based on whether or not /{organism}/xrefs/{systemCode}/{identifier} would possibly return a {targetSystemCode} result given a {sourceSystemCode} query. This function basically combines the results of /{organism}/sourceDataSources and /{organism}/targetDataSources into a single boolean result.
Returns the list of properties available for a given organism

200.description: Returns the list of properties available for a given organism

get.description: Returns a list of xrefs with identifiers that contain the query string for a given organism. Results are not restricted to exact matches. Optionally limit results to a specified number per data source.

parameters.description: Number of results per data source
parameters.name: limit

200.description: Returns a tab-delimited list of xrefs with identifiers that contain the query string for a given organism

get.description: Returns a list of data sources available as xref sources for a given organism.

get.description: Returns a list of data sources available as xref targets for a given organism.
